Astera Labs (NASDAQ: ALAB) provides rack-scale AI infrastructure through purpose-built connectivity solutions. By collaborating with hyperscalers and ecosystem partners, Astera Labs enables organizations to unlock the full potential of modern AI. As a **Physical Design & CAD Engineer**, you will serve as a Technical Lead developing Astera Labs' next-generation connectivity ASICs for cloud and AI infrastructure.

* Improve design quality, automation, and flow efficiency.

* Experience developing or maintaining Physical Design CAD flows.
* Hands-on experience with PNR, timing closure, and physical design signoff.
* Proficiency in Python and/or Tcl scripting.
* Experience with Cadence and/or Synopsys physical design tools.
* Experience with advanced semiconductor process nodes (7nm or below).

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Experience with 3nm or more advanced process technologies.
* Experience building automated CAD flows from synthesis through signoff.
* Familiarity with Cadence Innovus, Tempus, Genus, Synopsys ICC2, Fusion Compiler, and PrimeTime.
* Experience with EM/IR analysis, DRC/LVS, ECO, and timing signoff methodologies.
* Experience with block-level ownership through tapeout.

Situated in Stanford’s highly dynamic research environment, the Division of Clinical Informatics is seeking a Research Data Analyst to contribute to our research program focused on clinically applied machine learning, foundation models and multi-center observational studies. The successful candidate will work closely with researchers, data scientists and clinical/domain experts to prepare and analyze complex datasets, evaluate model performance, generate meaningful insights, and contribute to rigorous, reproducible research.

*The job duties listed below are typical examples of work performed by positions in this job classification and are not designed to contain or be interpreted as a comprehensive inventory of all duties, tasks, and responsibilities. Specific duties and responsibilities may vary depending on department or program needs without changing the general nature and scope of the job or level of responsibility.*

**Duties include:**

* Collect, manage and clean datasets.
* Employ new and existing tools to interpret, analyze, and visualize multivariate relationships in data.
* Develop algorithms and statistical models, and perform statistical analyses appropriate to data and reporting requirements.
* Use system reports and analyses to identify potentially problematic data and determine root cause for data problems
* Develop reports, charts, graphs and tables for use by investigators and for publication and presentation.
* Collaborate with faculty and research staff on data collection and analysis methods.
* Provide documentation based on audit and reporting criteria to investigators and research staff.
* Contribute to the development of a research program centered on machine learning with an initial focus on data from electronic health records
* Develop and evaluate machine learning models and reproducible end-to-end analytical pipelines using hospital data, including appropriate quality control and bias assessment
* Contribute technical expertise to program development activities, including research proposals, project planning, and stakeholder engagement.
* Coordinate and support knowledge sharing, documentation, and dissemination of methods and best practices within the research community
Support single- and multicenter observational research using the OMOP Common Data Model, including cohort development, quality assessment, and reproducible analysis.  

The ideal candidate for this position is an individual with knowledge of clinical data, sense of curiosity, attention to detail, quality analysis and validation methodologies, and strong interpersonal skills needed to work collaboratively with technical and non-technical stakeholders within and outside the Stanford research community, including faculty, researchers, clinicians, hospital administrators, engineering teams, IT staff and research coordinators.

**What to expect during the interview process:**

A typical interview process consists of resume screening, phone screenings, group and/or 1:1 interviews via zoom, reference and background checks. You may be required to demonstrate proof of programming and writing abilities. Interview candidates should expect to meet with other researchers, faculty, data scientists and software engineers.

**Resources:**

* Division of Clinical Informatics: https://med.stanford.edu/peds-clinical-informatics.html

* Research IT Website: https://med.stanford.edu/sdsr/research-technology.html

* STARR: https://starr.stanford.edu/

OHDSI CDM: https://www.ohdsi.org/data-standardization/the-common-data-%20model/

*\* - Other duties may also be assigned*

**DESIRED QUALIFICATIONS:**

* Experience developing and implementing algorithms for the processing of large datasets.
* Background in computer science, engineering or a related field with a strong understanding of statistics and scientific research
* Excellent project and time management skills and strong attention to detail
* Ability to work collaboratively with stakeholders across a large institution
* Outstanding problem solving and analytical skills
* Excellent writing skills to help with development of grants and papers
* Proficiency in SQL, Python and shell scripting
* Ability to work independently and in a diverse team environment
* Excellent verbal and written communication skills along with strong interpersonal skills
* Demonstrated creativity and latitude in problem solving, including the ability to prioritize and execute multiple competing tasks

  

**Core Duties** :

* Collect, manage and clean datasets.
* Employ new and existing tools to interpret, analyze, and visualize multivariate relationships in data.
* Create databases and reports, develop algorithms and statistical models, and perform statistical analyses appropriate to data and reporting requirements.
* Use system reports and analyses to identify potentially problematic data, make corrections, and determine root cause for data problems from input errors or inadequate field edits, and suggest possible solutions.
* Develop reports, charts, graphs and tables for use by investigators and for publication and presentation.
* Analyze data processes in documentation.
* Collaborate with faculty and research staff on data collection and analysis methods.
* Provide documentation based on audit and reporting criteria to investigators and research staff.
* Communicate with government officials, grant agencies and industry representatives.

**Minimum Education** :

Bachelor's degree or a combination of education and relevant experience.

**Minimum Experience** :

Experience in a quantitative discipline such as economics, finance, statistics or engineering.

**Knowledge, Skills and Abilities** :

* Substantial experience with MS Office and analytical programs.
* Strong writing and analytical skills.
* Ability to prioritize workload.

jobs.description:
E11 Bio is on a mission to advance connectomics towards the scale of whole mammalian brains. We are a collaborative and interdisciplinary team of scientists and engineers engaged in a neuroscience moonshot project to develop a radical technology platform for scalable brain mapping. E11 Bio is a non-profit Convergent Research focused research organization located in Alameda, California, pursuing blue-skies neuroscience research yet operating like a nimble, tight-knit start-up. Read our technology roadmap.

We are seeking a mission-aligned scientist or engineer who is equally comfortable at the bench, the microscope, and with quantitative data analysis. This role combines sample preparation, advanced microscopy, quantitative image analysis, with engineering-driven technology development focused on quick iterative troubleshooting and standardizing and automating protocols. You will collaborate closely with molecular biology, imaging, and computational teams to ensure we consistently prepare high quality specimens to support our ambitious scaling goals towards whole-brain connectomics.

The role forms a critical part of our sample production pipeline and will be responsible for expansion microscopy development and iteratively improving protocols. Your work will drive two overarching outcomes: improving gel performance and improving the quality, reproducibility and scalability of sample production. This combines hands-on experimental work with defining quantitative metrics to assess mechanical and optical gel properties, image quality and pipeline throughput.

### **Responsibilities**

* Independently design, coordinate, and execute bench level experiments focused on expansion microscopy.
* Operate within our sample production pipeline to ensure a continuous flow of high-quality gels
* Iteratively optimize expansion microscopy workflows by designing, sourcing and adapting techniques and methodologies from the literature and scientific community
* Pilot variations of expansion microscopy protocols focused on optimizing signal retention for multi-round cycles of immunostaining, imaging, and signal extinction.
* Pilot methods for increasing diffusion within expanded hydrogel/tissue hybrids. Pilot commercially available devices (e.g. ultrasound or microwave) and design custom built devices (in collaboration with external vendors) to facilitate these experiments.
* Work closely with experimental and computational scientists to collaboratively design experiments, analyze experimental data, and interpret results.
* Maintain excellent laboratory notebook practices, communicate results through reports and presentations, and contribute to and assist in preparation of manuscripts, abstracts and other scientific documents.

### **Required Qualifications**

* Ph.D. in biology, chemistry, bioengineering, materials science, mechanical engineering, or a related field, or equivalent research or industry experience
* Strong track record of end-to-end experimental ownership.
* Experience developing methods or protocols, ideally involving hydrogel chemistry, expansion microscopy, immunohistochemistry, or tissue processing
* Excellent communication and collaboration skills, with strong record-keeping practices and attention to reproducibility.

### **Preferred Qualifications**

* Experience working with advanced optical microscope modalities (e.g., spinning-disc confocal or light-sheet microscopy).
* Experience designing or applying quantitative scoring systems for expansion microscopy or imaging data
* Experience with scaling expansion microscopy throughput in routine production environments
* Experience automating lab workflows (e.g., liquid handlers, microcontrollers like Arduino or Raspberry Pi, scripting in Python)

Strong engineers new to these techniques are encouraged to apply, as are creative experimentalists from outside neuroscience who have developed expansion microscopy or similar methods in other fields. We’re looking for self-starters that iterate quickly and find creative, practical solutions to complex problems. Experience working in fast paced startup-like research environments where roles span multiple technical domains is preferred.

### **In 6 months, you will have:**

* Fully onboarded into the E11 production pipeline and be consistently generating high-quality gels for imaging
* Identify and standardize expansion microscopy QC metrics (e.g, measuring mechanical or optical properties) and stage gate thresholds, and integrated their routine measurement into the pipeline
* Increased production gel yield by 50% without a reduction in quality

### **In 12 months, you will have:**

* Improved the quality, reproducibility, and scalability of the pipeline, both in throughput and in the physical sample sizes we can process (for example, by developing methods for high-quality whole-brain gelation and expansion)
* Increased the reproducibility of our protocols so that technical variability between and within samples processed in parallel is reduced by 50%
* Reduced hands-on protocol time while improving outcomes and reproducibility, for example through in-house automation development or automation partnerships.

### **We offer**

* An opportunity to help change the world and work with a world-class interdisciplinary team of scientists and engineers on a field-defining moonshot
* Excellent medical, dental, and vision insurance through a PPO plan; parental leave.
* Generous time off + paid holidays.
* 401K matching up to 6% of base salary
* Ample healthy and energizing food including daily lunches.
* Stipend for fitness and wellness activities.

Bonus: Performance-based, up to 20% of base salary

jobs.title: Research Associate, Applied Cell Line Development & Customer Programs
jobs.description:
Prolific Machines is ushering in a new era of biotechnology with light. Our first-of-its-kind optogenetic platform delivers unprecedented control, precisely guiding cellular behavior when and where it matters most. Unlike existing tools used to control biology, our technology enables dynamic, tunable control over virtually any cellular function in any cell type. We're enabling partners to unlock robust efficiency, quality, and reproducibility advantages across the most complex pharmaceuticals and therapeutic proteins. Prolific is supported by leading investors, including Bill Gates’s Breakthrough Energy Ventures, Mayfield and SOSV.

We are looking for a motivated and detail-oriented Research Associate to help advance our mammalian cell line development and protein production capabilities. At Prolific, we use light to control the expression of biotherapeutic proteins, with the goal of increasing titer and improving quality attributes. In this role, you will play a key part in generating and characterizing cell lines that support both internal research and customer programs. The ideal candidate enjoys hands-on laboratory work, takes pride in delivering consistent, high-quality results, and is eager to learn and grow in a fast-paced startup environment. You’ll collaborate with scientists and engineers across multiple disciplines, with opportunities to expand your technical expertise, take on increasing ownership, and contribute directly to Prolific’s success. This role is based on-site in our headquarters in Emeryville, CA.

### **Responsibilities:**

* Own and drive workflows using mammalian cell culture, primarily working with suspension HEK and suspension CHO
* Generate stable cell lines via transfection (ie electroporation) and selection as well as serving as the primary technical owner of many genetically distinct cell lines at once
* Handle protein production workflows at different scales - deep well plates and shake flasks, potentially including small scale bioreactors such as the Ambr system
* Execute downstream readouts such as cell counting (Celleca, nucleocounter), metabolite measurements (Nova / CEDEX), Octet BLI, flow cytometry
* Perform single cell isolation using methods such as FACS, cell deposition, or Beacon
* Execute plasmid cloning and molecular biology techniques including PCR and ddPCR
* Conduct experiments independently, collect and analyze data in a timely manner, maintain detailed documentation in electronic lab notebooks, and data visualization and presentation in team meetings

### **Requirements:**

* Bachelor's degree in Biology, Bioengineering, Biotechnology, or a related field, with relevant laboratory experience in mammalian cell culture. Candidates will be considered at the Research Associate I, Research Associate II, and Senior Research Associate levels based on their experience, technical proficiency, and demonstrated independence.
* Proficient in mammalian cell culture, preferably with experience in cell line development, and are well versed in sterile technique, transfection, and clone isolation

* Execute downstream readouts such as cell counting (Celleca, nucleocounter), metabolite measurements (Nova / CEDEX), Octet BLI, flow cytometry

The Merchant lab seeks a Research Associate with and interest in cancer biology and tumor immunology. Studies in the lab make use of mouse models to examine the tumor immunology, with correlation in human patient samples. The studies are part of an NIH funded project aiming to increase our understanding of resistance of non-Hodgkin’s lymphoma (NHL) to chemotherapy and immunotherapy.
